ratings.comment: Worst professor I've ever had. Blames students for bad exam grades, never returned any of project grades. Nobody knew how they were doing in the class until the final grades were posted.
WORST TEACHER EVER. DO NOT TAKE HIM FOR ANY CLASS.

The subject is not horrible with him but you need to go to lecture because he adds a lot to the slides during lecture. What he writes on the white board has a VERY high chance of being on the exams. He gives 'study guides' that are quiet vague but if you find the answers then you are great for the test. Not entertaining but very knowledgable.

As a lecturer not that great. Seems like he hardly knows material while speaking during lecture but when you ask him questions during office hours or after class he gives really good concise and clear responses. Definitely knows his stuff just poor presenter/lecturer. Subject material is not difficult. Fairly easy class to pass.

Honestly, this is one of the best professors here in Cal State Long Beach. no idea why people are saying bad things about this professor. Yes, he makes the class difficult, really difficult. But his explanations are always accurate and concise. If you want to pass, you have to study before lecture; considering 229 is an abstract class. 326 is fun!

do not take this professor if possible. expect having to teach yourself the material on your own time. feedback is unhelpful, marks down correct answers because you didn't do it "his" way.  class average on exams are well below 50%, but that's obviously our fault, right?

This class made no logical sense how would you expect someone to pass a class when you get test/quizzes and , homework on material you haven't even learned yet. His teaching style is so robotic too with little to no emotion what so ever. 0/5 wouldn't meme again.

One of the most unorganized professor I have ever experienced. Unclear answers when students ask questions. Assign homework, quizzes, and exams on materials we have not touched yet. Do not take this guy.

Doesn't explain his lecture slides well. TRies to be funny in class, but the only thing funny was our grades when we get the results back. Lectures are unclear, quizes/tests are ridiculously hard, avoid if u can.

He pauses in between sentences which adds up to half the class time Spends a month lecturing half a chapter. During reviews, he goes over questions that won't be on the exam . Takes off points if you don't solve it the way he wants it. I should have listened to the previous reviews on this man. Please read the other reviews and avoid this man.

His class, tests, and quizzes are the definition of that one meme. Sally has four apples and gives one away.. calculate the mass of the sun.. like bruh Alot of college is self teaching/learning. But this class takes it to the next level. He lectures off slides with no additional context of HW problems. Very few examples and guidance given. avoid

Discrete Structures is a boring course made even more dry by Ratana Ngo's somewhat robotic teaching style. He really tries to make sure the class understands, but his presentation leaves many falling asleep.

Ratana tries his best & I respect that, but he still falls way short of being an effective professor for 229. This was his first time teaching 229 so I can only hope this was a result of inexperience of teaching this course. His lectures are unclear, unorganized, & he made frequent mistakes. He also posted our full names next to our grades & IDs

Speaks loudly and clearly, and is decent at conveying the material. However, he is unorganized, so the lab time tended to be done ad-hoc. But, this gives you tons of time to ask him questions if you're unsure of something. Also, despite assigning homework frequently, he only collected it as a large bundle twice, so you didn't get timely feedback.
one of the best teachers that i have.

His teaching style is not easy to adapt to. The concepts in the class are drowned out by his example problems and poor explanations. The guy "teaches" coding and algorithms yet doesn't have the ability to operate his laptop (which uses Win '98...).

I've found a technique to deal with prof like these: JUST REMEMBER YOU ARE AT A STATE COLLEGE. Enough said? You get what you pay for, even if cheap college isn't necessarily cheap. It's clear when a prof doesn't know the material they are teaching, but what isn't clear is why they expect you to know it. Input is Output so TEACH YOURSELF in upperdiv

The content of the class is not difficult. However, instead of teaching the basic concepts, he mostly uses his example problems and goes off on useless tangents, which only leads to class confusion, which leads to wasting time answering questions trying to justify himself. He never uses the book, but to get an A, I'd recommend reading it.

I was able to understand his lectures but his labs were pretty difficult for students that just learned about operating systems. His tests are extremely hard and based off only on lectures so take very good notes. Grades hard on labs. Overall just study your butt off and you'll pass the class.

Ratana is a pretty awful instructor who can struggles to explain the most basic concepts of operating systems. He recycles assignments, quizzes, and tests, and he teaches this class pretty often, so it shouldn't be difficult to find resources from previous semesters.

Took him for 326 and 327. The courses aren't the easiest, but Ratana is really relaxed about due dates and the assignments are doable, most are even easy. His lectures are clear and tests follow the lectures.

Helpful if you ask, but he has an impressively difficult time explaining the subject material to you, or is blatantly unable to do so. He tries his best to spend minimal effort for the class. Internet is a better resource. Also unforgivingly picky on tests, but a nice guy.

Ratana seems to put minimal effort into his class. Lectures are dull (which he is aware of and mentions every class) and his tests/quizzes are straight from his notes. Understand the code in his notes and you'll do fine in his tests (tests are barely curved). Labs are very reasonable and are graded fairly (he's picky about commenting though).

His lectures are very dull and he just reads it off the powerpoint.  But his class in general is very easy.  His tests are all open book, and he gives you the code for programs and asks you to make some small changes.  Ohh also,there is 4 weeks grace period on labs. Easy class but dont except to learn much.

this class was so boring, i was always falling asleep in this class. His lectures were based on power points ans drawings that he did on the board. the exams and quizzes were open notes so this made him a hard grader!!oh and one good but bad thing of this class is his 4 week grace period for labs!

He's a nice guy but his lectures are boring. You don't really need the textbook. If you get stuck, Google is a better resource. The tests are from the slides, so make sure you take notes during lecture. His labs are hard so start early. He gives you a 4-week grace period which can be bad for people who like to procrastinate.

Not a bad professor. He uses power point presentation everyday, which makes it hard to pay attention. He is however, extremely fair minded and reasonable when it comes to grading and tests. You really have to stay on top of the projects or they begin to pile up. The pace of the labs felt rather rushed towards the end of the semester.

This guy is infamous in the department for having poor knowledge of the material he is supposed to be teaching. That proved to be true this semester for operating systems. Terrible instructor and pretty bad personality. I don't recommend this guy at all! He should really should find another profession.

This professor is interesting. The more  questions he answers during lectures, the more his stupidity shows. He is not credible to teach this class. The CECS department really needs to stop assigning this class to Mr. Ngo.

Not a great teacher by any means, but not as bad as people make him out to be. He does communicate the information, but in such a roundabout way that it's hard to stay focused on what he's saying. Should be an easy A, just take good notes on lectures, study his review sheets well and you should be fine, and annotate his powerpoint slides.
Mr. Ngo is the worst instructor I have ever had, and I've had my share. He is unclear and not effective. He needs to find another career.
This guy is terrible. HE CAN'T TEACH!

Not very friendly - can be defensive when questioned, or will just decide to not help you. I had A's all semester, then received a B in the course. When I questioned him, he said I did horrible on the final. When I asked to see my final exam, my request was denied. Sub-standard to say the least.

He means well but his thought process makes things very difficult to understand. I want a professor who is extremely clear and seems to know the ins and outs to what he/she is teaching. I feel that Ngo is not clear and I did not feel that he was credible. VERY unorganized and I felt like the class was winged. If you like organization, stay away.

This guy was the most unorganized professor I have ever had. We started being surprised when he actually showed up on time. The 2nd exam was so poorly written that most people got C's. Had weekly papers (2 pages each), which were a pain to write. Lectures straight from the powerpoint, so just study those.

Disorganized and unprepared to teach the class. We literally had to teach ourselves the material. His lectures were almost useless and the labs were almost as frustrating. I passed but I might take it again with another professor before continuing.

He's very nice, and he obviously knows the material, but he doesn't do a good job teaching it. If you already understand the concepts, it's tedious. If you don't, you're out of luck. Homework and lectures are on Beachboard, you don't need to buy the book. You might get the solutions guide from amazon if are struggling, but it's not necessary.

An alright prof.  He's kind of boring, but you learn from him.  His labs can be tough, so start early.  His tests are mostly from his labs, so it is worth to at least understand how his labs should work.  I think he is an alright professor.
Excellent teacher. He uses power points, so the book is mostly unnecessary. He is very thorough in going over the subject. If you study well the code he gives you, the test will be easy.

He is a very boring professor who lectures from powerpoints every day.  The book is a nice reference, but unneeded given his notes.  His labs seem harder than usual, but they do help you learn the language.  His exams and quizzes are all coding questions, and they are not hard if you know the material.  He allows up to a page of notes for exams.

The most boring class that I have ever taken.  His Power point were based on the fifth edition of the Java textbook so you don't really have to purchase the book (currently it's at the 6th edition). Heck I won't blame you if you want to skip several class dates because of him.
****ing boring, avoid at all costs!!!
worest teacher ever took. useless in class and doesnt explain anything good.

Easy class, but he lectures from powerpoints every day and it gets very boring very fast. Nice thing about the powerpoints is he posts them on Beachboard so you don't have to come to class or take notes.  I'd take another class with him.
Changed my CS Minor track so I wouldn't have to take his class again.

He didn't do a good job of explaining confusing topics.  He was very tough about lab/project grading.  He'd take off points for very small cosmetic details on labs, projects, quizes and tests.  He lectures off PDF's everyday and it can get very boring.  He wouldn't be my first choice for a CECS professor, but I'd take him again if I had to.

I had 2 classes in the same semester with this guy a few years ago, and he did the strangest thing.  In the first class, he noticed that he had made a typo on the syllabus.  Then in the 2nd class, he used the same syllabus and pretended that he had just realized AGAIN that there was a typo.  Also, he sounds like the original Skeletor from He-Man.
You will only do well in his class if your answers match with what he wants... which may not necessarily from the book.
very boring, Ngo is a joke.. Needs to retire..

Very cool instructor....One of the best instructor there is. If having difficulty with assignments or tests...talk to him and he'll offer chances.. The best instructor you can have.... recomment him to anyone!
Good teacher, very nice guy. he gives you second chances on tests. lecutures are not that boring. easy going nice guy. no accent

Awesome class, I enjoyed it ! He gave us quizes instead of midterm,one page "cheat sheet" at every quiz. If you listen in class, quizes won't be hard. Labs and projects are super interesting, he allows you to use your own creativity to come up with a solution. Overall, an excellent professor!
Lectures could have been more clear, tests were from lecture, but he was a tough grader, projects were difficult but I learned a lot from them.

A bit hyperactive, not the clearest in the presentation of his lectures, and not good at all in preparing students for his labwork.  Grades exams very mercilessly, many times demanding regurgitation of his exact terminology and not even a very reasonable facsimile will do.

Explains everything very clearly, except his grading policy.  Watch the keywords, he's a real stickler for HIS terminology (by HIS, I don't mean the Almighty).  That said, I learned a lot in his class.

Sometimes has trouble communicating what he is trying to say.  Needs to have more complete notes for his lectures so he doesn't waste so much time in class.  Tends to spend too much time on the same example.  Projects/tests are fair, overall an ok teacher
